analyst_view.overall: Celta (27th, 3 points) host Bournemouth (2nd, 12 points from four wins) at Balaidos. Bournemouth under Marco Rose have won nine in a row in all competitions and Evanilson has scored in five straight games, but Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Juanlu Sanchez are out (all in the numbers' missing list), and previews expect some rotation, possibly a rest for Evanilson with Kroupi starting, before Sunday's trip to Fulham. Celta lost 2-1 at Real Madrid, have scored once at home in almost 300 minutes and Claudio Giraldez is under pressure; striker Borja Iglesias (calf) and Miguel Roman (knee) are still out and Carl Starfelt is close, none of them in the numbers' missing list, while local press expects Carreira, Hugo Alvarez and Pablo Duran to be rested with Villarreal coming on Sunday. German referee Harm Osmers books a little more than average, which the numbers count. I keep a small lean lower on goals for Celta's blunt attack and Bournemouth's likely changes up front; the rest stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). Borja Iglesias, their main striker, is still out and not in the missing list, and Bournemouth may rest Evanilson, their in-form scorer; since much of Iglesias' absence already shows in Celta's form, I only go mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, split fairly evenly. Bournemouth's direct, wide play and Celta's wing-backs both produce corners, and recent corner form is already in the numbers, so rotation on either side does not clearly change this. I stay at about 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised 13% for referee Harm Osmers (4.5 a game) and lowered for Bournemouth's few recent bookings. Yoel Lago's ban is for Celta's league game, not this one, and Bafode Diakite is one booking from a Europa League ban, which may make him careful; nothing suggests a heated match, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.4%), even if few go in. Rotation on both sides (Kroupi for Evanilson, fresh legs for Celta) changes faces more than volume, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which partly reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth's forward line keeps their side up even if Evanilson rests, so I stay at about 8.8.
